title: Looking for tools for ai art for project already in progress
author: frenchy3
selftext: I have a side project I have been working on for about 2.5 years. I had some artists help me at certain points but they all left to do other things, leaving me with a game that is about half finished. I want to use ai to generate the remaining assets, but I'm new to ai. I'm making a top down 2D game pixel art game with gameboy advance style graphics. Ideally, I'm looking for an ai I can give my art as references and then have it generate new art in the same style and pallet. My characters in the game only have simple up/left/down/right walking animations and the enemies have a 10 frame simple animation where they move around a little bit, so nothing crazy there. I'm also curious about how much it would cost as an estimate. I live in Japan and the USD to yen conversion is not good. I need about 100 more monsters and 10-15 characters, so I do not want to spend a couple thousand dollars. Thanks in advance for any answers.

replies.author: frenchy3
replies.body: Thanks for the recommendation. I checked out the website, but I do not see anything showing pixel art or games. How is it useful for my situation?

replies.author: Technical-County-727
replies.body: I would assume it can do you pixel art, but def. not game ready stuff

comments.author: ND_Jamoose
comments.body: It really depends on directions, animations, frames. 100 monsters can reach an extremely high price.  If it's just static images with no directions and animations you can probably do it with ai. If the art style is very retro it will not be easy. Anyway you need to provide more details with regard to what exactly you want to create.

replies.author: frenchy3
replies.body: The art style is gameboy advance games like Pokemon or Zelda. The battles are turned based with a side view of the monsters and they have simple animations like moving their head and blinking or moving up and down.

replies.author: ND_Jamoose
replies.body: Try MagicPixel for creating variations of an existing reference image. If I was you, I'd forget about the animations and just move the sprites when they attack like in oldschool pokemon. Before Crystal I believe, there were no animations at all, only when you quick attack for example, the sprite of the pokemon itself is moved forward, etc.

replies.author: frenchy3
replies.body: I probably have to end up doing this, but I have 70 monsters in the game with animations so it would have been nice to have animations for all of them. Initially, it was just a static image, but the artist who was helping me wanted to add the animations, then he got a job and left the project lol.

comments.author: J0joBean
comments.body: Pixel art? U wanna mess with pixlab/pixelorama, or aesprite. Pixlab as their own ai says, aesprite u can integrate Claude/etc to help create/animate.

comments.author: meatballpiggy
comments.body: Chat GPT just upgraded to 5.4 and I feel it really improved in pixel art. You get a decent amount of free generations a day and if you don’t want to pay you can just make multiple Gmail accounts. Pixel lab.ai specializes in pixel art and has a discord to help as well as some YouTube tutorials. Gemini is alright too but sometimes it’s hit or miss

replies.author: frenchy3
replies.body: Thank you. I will check it out. Can I provide reference images with chat gpt?

replies.author: ND_Jamoose
replies.body: Yes. But make sure to tell it what you don't want. It tends to upscale and add details so you need to tell it things like don't upscale, don't add details, don't make in modern style, etc, alongside what you do want to see of course.

comments.author: beelllllll
comments.body: Autosprite.io can do what you are asking

replies.author: frenchy3
replies.body: I've tried this before and the results were actually terrible. I gave it a start and end frame of my character and asked for 4 frames of animation with a very detailed description. The results were basically unusable and the art had artifacts all around it that would require serious work from an artist. I tried making 5 characters than gave up on it.

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body: Ahh yes it shines more at 25 frames, the better approach for this is actually to do 25 frame (or more), and then in the editor 'choose' your best 4 frames.

replies.author: frenchy3
replies.body: Oh this is good to know, thank you.
